transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

If you're not sure about the specific instructions for your eye gel, I'd recommend checking with your GP or pharmacist to confirm.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense. I do have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the advice. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but this should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How many days or weeks have passed since your surgery? That will help me give you a better answer.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about two weeks since my surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Thank you for letting me know. By two weeks, your vision should be improving, though it may not be perfectly clear yet. Some blurriness at this stage is still fairly common as your eyes continue to settle.

However, if your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. 

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! Before we finish, can I just confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you so much!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!

verdict.label: pass
